jobs.title: Senior Infrastructure Engineer
jobs.description:
First and most importantly: our mission is to bring transparency and clarity to the world's data.

Our platform, FiftyOne, is where AI work happens. Our enterprise platform is the mission critical linchpin for managing unstructured data, model development, and AI systems at the world's largest companies.

We believe that open source is the way to lead the data-centric AI revolution. Our open source version has 4 million downloads to-date.

Our software massively impacts AI work across almost every vertical: from self-driving cars to medical imaging to revolutionizing agriculture, we are at the thrilling center of real-world AI advancement’s next wave.

And we’re built on three key tenets:

• We are all human beings: we strive to be a “human-first” organization and treat everyone with the respect, care, and flexibility that all people deserve.

• We are distributed: we believe in getting autonomy and power into the hands of people actually doing the work.

• We believe in the power of community.

We are fully remote, hiring for people based in the United States, and who are prepared to travel to at least 2 in-person retreats per year.

About your role

As a Senior Infrastructure Engineer at Voxel51, you will shape the architecture and strategy of the systems that power our platform — from individual researchers to enterprise-scale deployments. You’ll lead the design of containerized systems, CI/CD pipelines, and deployment solutions across cloud and on-premises environments, while solving the unique challenges of serving unstructured data (images and video) at scale.

You’ll partner with enterprise customers, guiding and troubleshooting their production deployments. You’ll collaborate across engineering teams to improve developer productivity, and mentor peers while setting infrastructure best practices. Your work will directly shape the reliability, security, and scalability of Voxel51’s platform — and accelerate our mission to democratize data-centric ML.

What you will do

• Shape the architecture and evolution of Voxel51’s infrastructure to support deployments ranging from individual researchers to Fortune 500 enterprises

• Design, build, and scale deployment systems across cloud (GCP, AWS, Azure) and on-premises environments, ensuring reliability, security, and repeatability

• Partner with enterprise customers (and our Customer Success Machine Learning Engineers) to deliver and support production-grade deployments in their environments, guiding them through installation, troubleshooting, and scaling

• Lead infrastructure initiatives across engineering teams, enabling peers to develop, test, and ship features faster with robust internal tooling and automation

• Drive best practices in CI/CD, evolving our pipelines (currently GitHub Actions + Google Cloud Build) and introducing new approaches where they add value

• Develop and maintain deployment solutions for Voxel51-hosted environments (GKE) as well as customer on-prem installations (K8s or Docker Compose)

• Champion developer productivity, improving workflows for development and automated cloud deployments

• Troubleshoot and resolve complex infrastructure issues, spanning build failures, runtime failures, and customer deployment challenges

• Anticipate and prevent failures by designing monitoring, alerting, and predictive solutions for both internal and customer environments

• Mentor engineers and set technical direction, ensuring Voxel51’s infrastructure remains ahead of customer needs and industry trends

What you should bring

• Deep experience with containerized environments

• Building, packaging, and debugging container images

• Kubernetes (and Docker Compose) for orchestration

• Building, maintaining, and deploying Helm charts

• Infrastructure as Code expertise (Terraform, Ansible, or equivalent)

• Scripting and automation skills (Bash or similar)

• Python expertise, including build and environment management, packaging/distribution, release management, and dependency debugging

• CI/CD systems experience, ideally GitHub Actions (we use this today)

• Cloud infrastructure knowledge, especially GCP (IAM, VPC, load balancing, ingress/egress routing, proxies, firewall rules)

• Database fundamentals, ideally MongoDB or similar NoSQL systems

• Observability skills, including designing meaningful monitors, logging, tracing, and alerting

• Security best practices, including certificates, service accounts, least privilege, and role assumptions

• Troubleshooting ability across complex, distributed systems (including with customers in the loop)

• Testing mindset: comfortable with designing and applying different types of tests to validate functionality

• Strong communication skills, with the ability to work directly with enterprise customers as well as collaborate across teams in a remote-first, collaborative environment

• Adaptability and curiosity, with the ability to ramp quickly on unfamiliar concepts and technologies

The cash compensation for this person is in the $210K - $240K range. In addition to base comp for this role, we offer equity in the form of options, a variety of benefits, and the opportunity to grow in an exciting and collaborative environment.

jobs.title: General Counsel
jobs.description:
ABOUT US

Sydecar is on a mission to transform the world of private markets. Our goal is to make these markets more accessible, transparent, and liquid, and we're achieving this by revolutionizing the way investment vehicles are created and executed.



At Sydecar, we're not just a platform; we're a trusted partner in venture capital. We're dedicated to simplifying and standardizing the private investing experience, empowering capital allocators to discover and support visionary entrepreneurs who are shaping the future.



Our platform is designed with ease and efficiency in mind. We take care of all the behind-the-scenes tasks, from automating banking, ensuring compliance, handling contracts, managing taxes, to streamlining reporting. This leaves investors the freedom to concentrate on what matters most: making valuable deals and nurturing meaningful relationships.



Join us at Sydecar, as we lead the charge in revolutionizing private investing.


ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY

The core mission of the executive team is to execute an ambitious roadmap to build the most intuitive, compliant, and stable method of executing alternative asset investments. Our General Counsel will keep our products compliant while helping us push the boundaries of what's possible, finding the path to yes on novel product ideas rather than defaulting to no.

As General Counsel you will span legal research, thought leadership, and product innovation, adding value across every aspect of our operation. Reporting to the CEO and serving as a strategic advisor to the CEO and VP of Product, you will ensure our suite of products and services meets the highest standards of federal, state, and international compliance, while exploring creative ways to reduce friction for our users and keep our team on the cutting edge of the industry.



WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

 - Lead, manage, and continue building a multidisciplinary legal and compliance team.

 - Analyze legal issues through risk assessment, risk management, and pragmatic decision-making lenses and provide actionable solutions, rather than simply identifying areas of potential legal risk.

 - Work on a range of matters such as securities and regulatory compliance, negotiating, reviewing, and drafting commercial agreements.

 - Advise executive members on changes in law, regulation, and best practices that impact the business.

 - Build and maintain a referenceable knowledge base to educate our stakeholders with respect to: Why our products are designed the way they are. Why do we use specific language in our product. What laws affect the business.

 - Contribute directly to innovative fund structures and shape Sydecar’s current and future products.

 - Track evolving regulatory frameworks affecting alternative asset investing and, where appropriate, engage with industry groups and policymakers to help shape them.

 - Field and respond to external inquiries regarding our business.

 - Manage outside counsel, as necessary.
   


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Experience building and scaling legal teams inside fast-growing organizations.

 - Experience partnering closely with product teams, where legal input directly shaped product decisions and outcomes.

 - Strong written and verbal communicator who can flex between board-level summaries and in-the-weeds deal negotiation.

 - Excellent strategic thinking, solid judgment, and the willingness to work with business partners to make decisions that are grounded in a practical application of the law, the technology, and the business goals.

 - Ability to work under pressure in a fast-paced, innovative, rapidly changing environment, and get up to speed on new areas of law quickly and effectively, and comfortably in a startup business environment.

 - A JD from an ABA-accredited law school and an active bar license in good standing with 10+ years of legal practice experience and extensive in-house experience in the FinTech or venture capital space.

 - Strongly preferred: deep expertise in the range of securities laws impacting venture funds and FinTech platforms, including the Securities Act, Exchange Act, Investment Company Act, Investment Advisers Act, and FINRA Rules.


SYDECAR’S VALUES

Our values are important to the way we live and work at Sydecar. They guide our priorities, behaviors and interactions.

Be Committed

As a team, we rise to meet challenges and recognize that we become stronger and develop character when facing adversity.

Be Excellent

We measure our success not just by what we achieve, but by how we achieve it—through integrity, creativity, elegance, and a commitment to continuous improvement. Excellence is not just doing things well—it's looking for ways to do them better.

Be Humble

Humility is our key to personal and professional growth. We appreciate that great ideas can come from anywhere, regardless of seniority, pedigree, or experience. We care more about collective outcomes than who gets credit or who does what. We try to not let our ego cloud our judgment.

Win Together

Winning is no accident. It is the result of collective hard work, perseverance, sacrifice, and most of all, loving what we do. Winning requires that we give extra—sometimes winning calls for late nights or extra effort, and we show up for clients and each other with urgency and heart. While excellence is a journey, winning is a destination.



Sydecar is committed to the principle of equal employment opportunity for all employees and to providing employees with a work environment free of discrimination and harassment. All employment decisions at Sydecar are based on business needs, job requirements and individual qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion or belief, national, social or ethnic origin, sex (including pregnancy), age, physical, mental or sensory disability, HIV Status, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, marital, civil union or domestic partnership status, past or present military service, family medical history or genetic information, family or parental status, or any other status protected by the laws or regulations in the locations where we operate. Sydecar will not tolerate discrimination or harassment based on any of these characteristics. Sydecar encourages applicants of all ages.

jobs.title: Forward Deployed Data Engineer - Latin America
jobs.description:
ABOUT DATAFOLD

Datafold is the data engineering automation platform. A major part of our business is delivering large-scale data engineering projects such as data platform migrations with AI, at fixed price and guaranteed timeline. We are not a typical services provider or SI – we are a venture-backed software company that reimagined automation from the ground up and has been delivering projects up to 6x faster than alternatives.

We partner heavily with leading data platforms, including Databricks and Snowflake, to deliver large-scale complex migrations.


ABOUT THE ROLE

Datafold is hiring a Forward Deployed Data Engineer to own the delivery of our AI-automated data platform migration projects. This is a high-ownership, customer-facing role at the intersection of data engineering, AI, and project leadership.

As a Forward Deployed Data Engineer leveraging Datafold's AI technology, you will own migration projects end-to-end, gain deep understanding of the customer's data platform, manage execution of the project, and remove any blockers on the way for a timely migration delivery.

Using our proprietary AI tooling to plan and deliver the migration projects, you will be doing the work equivalent to a full team of consultants.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own 1–4 concurrent migration projects end-to-end: scoping, planning, execution, and customer handoff

 - Be the primary customer contact: run weekly check-ins, manage stakeholder expectations, and escalate risks early before they compound

 - Configure Datafold's Migration Agent and oversee the migration execution

 - Partner with Datafold's engineering team to execute migrations

 - Help refine and scale our product and delivery playbook as the team grows


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 3–6 years in data consulting, professional services, or a customer-facing data engineering role

Sitting at the intersection of markets, product, and customer experience, our team combines rigorous investment thinking with a mobile-first product design. jobs.title: Electrical Engineering Intern - Summer 2027
jobs.description:
About Us

At Antares, our long-term mission is to make clean energy abundant from Earth to the Asteroid Belt. We’re fueled by the belief that advanced nuclear energy can strengthen our military, solve the climate crisis, elevate global living standards, and expand humanity's presence in outer space. To achieve our mission, we’re building mass-producible, inherently safe, deployable microreactors that can be used terrestrially, underwater, and in space.



The Antares team hails from SpaceX, the White House, the Pentagon, the Department of Energy, MIT, Rigetti Computing, General Atomics, Relativity Space, Ursa Major, and National Laboratories like Idaho, Oak Ridge, Los Alamos, and Savannah River. Antares has raised over $600M in venture capital from top-tier investors and has hundreds of million-dollars on contract with the military services, NASA, and the Department of Energy.




ABOUT THE SUMMER INTERNSHIP PROGRAM



Internships at Antares are anything but ordinary. You'll work alongside our team as we design, build, and test fission microreactors built to deliver reliable energy for critical missions on Earth, in space, and underwater.



Our interns contribute to real work from day one. Depending on your role, you may touch hardware, write and test software, support manufacturing and operations, or help build the systems that allow Antares to move quickly as we scale. You'll work alongside engineers, operators, and other experts solving challenging problems—and you'll leave your internship with hands-on experience that's difficult to find anywhere else.



We work hard, move quickly, and take pride in what we're building. If you're excited to learn by doing and want to contribute to the next generation of nuclear energy, we'd love to have you join us next summer.



We will be running two separate cohorts to accommodate students on both semester and quarter schedules:

Cohort #1

Monday, May 17 – Friday, August 13

Cohort #2

Monday, June 14 – Friday, September 10



All internship roles are based at our Torrance headquarters and require interns to work onsite five days per week. We will not be considering candidates for remote or hybrid arrangements. Interns will receive a relocation and housing stipend as part of their offer package.



About the Team

Antares is developing compact nuclear reactors to deliver reliable power in the world’s most demanding environments. We’re looking for an Electrical Engineering Intern to support the design and testing of the electrical systems that make those reactors work.



You will begin with focused starter projects before taking ownership of a longer-term project culminating in a technical deliverable and presentation. Interns are integrated into the engineering team and evaluated with expectations similar to those of a first-year junior engineer. The bar for success is high: you will be expected to use your mentor and available resources effectively, execute independently, communicate clearly, and identify additional issues and opportunities for improvement.



Roles and Responsibilities:

 - Redesign printed circuit board assemblies (PCBAs) for new reactor systems

 - Develop schematics, select components, and support PCB layout and design reviews

 - Design electrical harnesses, including wiring diagrams, connector selection, pinouts, and routing

 - Build and test prototype boards, harnesses, and electrical assemblies

 - Develop and execute hardware-in-the-loop (HITL) tests

 - Support the buildout of system-level test infrastructure for hardware qualification.

 - Troubleshoot electrical hardware and identify root causes of failures

 - Analyze test data and recommend design improvements

 - Create clear design, test, and configuration documentation

 - Work closely with electrical, mechanical, controls, and test engineers to integrate designs into larger systems



Basic Qualifications:

 - Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, or a related field

 - Familiarity with circuit design, schematics, and PCB development

 - Experience building, testing, or debugging electrical hardware through coursework, a student team, research, or personal projects

 - Understanding of common electrical test equipment, such as oscilloscopes, multimeters, power supplies, and logic analyzers

 - Ability to read electrical drawings, datasheets, and technical documentation

 - Strong problem-solving skills and a willingness to work directly with hardware

 - Clear written and verbal communication



Preferred Skills & Experience:

 - Experience with Altium Designer or another PCB design tool

 - Experience designing cable harnesses or selecting connectors

 - Familiarity with embedded systems, microcontrollers, or common communication protocols

 - Experience with hardware-in-the-loop testing or automated test systems

 - Familiarity with Python, MATLAB, LabVIEW, or similar test and analysis tools

 - Experience working on a Formula SAE, rocketry, robotics, CubeSat, or other hands-on engineering team



Location

 - We are located in Torrance, CA in a 322,000 square foot, brand new facility featuring large open spaces for team collaboration, R&D, and production, as well as easy access to the 405, 105, and 110 freeways. Our facility is in the heart of Los Angeles' vibrant emerging tech ecosystem alongside many other high growth startups and enterprises.



Culture

At Antares, we like to specifically tie each role to our founding document’s set of values–here are the top five cultural values we think you should believe at your core to be successful:

 - Think in Systems - Energy and Defense are complex ecosystems with numerous stakeholders with competing priorities, conflicting policies, perverse incentives, and emergent and path-dependent properties. First principles thinking alone is insufficient. Think probabilistically and then take action. “If you want to be certain, then you are apt to be obsolete.” Over-optimizing the components often degrades the system

 - Obsess over the End User - The customer and end user are often not the same. We will never build globally competitive commercial products if we lose sight of our end users and their entire interaction with the product life cycle

 - Be Unconstrained by Convention - Our only limits are the laws of physics. Many, even experts, will say what we are working on is impossible. They said the same about SpaceX reusing rockets. Generationally impactful companies, by definition, must accomplish the seemingly impossible. If it were easy, it would have already been done. Never shy away from a solution because it has never been tried before, and never choose to do something because that's “how it's always been done”

 - Go Where the Work Is - Never miss a chance to meet a customer, user, or stakeholder face to face, even if that means hopping on a plane. If you can’t make it, find a teammate who can channel your intentions and go in your place. Deep work can be done from anywhere, but we believe teams are built in person, and aim to maximize our time together

 - Operate in the Grey - Embrace nuance in pursuit of truth. Question every fundamental assumption
   
   

Equal Opportunity

Antares is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are based solely on merit, competence, and qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability, or any other legally protected status.




ITAR REQUIREMENTS

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. jobs.title: Senior ML Engineer
jobs.description:
About the team

The Security and Risk Engineering organization builds scalable, AI-powered security solutions that reduce risk and protect ServiceNow and its customers. We value AI-first thinking, clean architecture, intuitive experiences, and a culture of continuous learning.

This is a zero-to-one incubation. We’re building a new class of exposure analysis that ranks security work by exploitability—where an attacker could realistically get in—rather than raw severity. The architecture is evolving, and this role helps define what good looks like.

The role

As a Senior ML Engineer, you build core components of a novel exploitability engine—shipping production ML that turns raw security signal into ranked, reachable attack paths. You take well-scoped problems from design to production and grow into deeper ownership as the system matures.

What you’ll own

• Well-scoped components of the engine—evidence ingestion and connectors, entity resolution, graph construction, or parts of the probability core—built to production quality.
• The correctness and reliability of what you ship: tests, evaluation, observability, and the metrics that show your component works.
• Turning ambiguous requirements into working code, with guidance on the calls that shape the wider system.
• The data and model plumbing that keeps the graph accurate—entity-resolution quality, evidence provenance, and decay.

What you’ll do

• Design, build, test, and operate production ML components with strong engineering fundamentals.
• Contribute to design and code reviews, and help raise the quality bar on the team.
• Prototype quickly to evaluate new AI capabilities against real cybersecurity problems.
• Partner with product, security R&D, and SecOps to understand the problem behind the ticket.
• Apply AI safety, security, and guardrail practices to what you build.

What you bring

• Solid software engineering fundamentals and experience operating production-quality software.
• Hands-on experience building ML- or LLM-powered applications—RAG, embeddings, agents, or probabilistic or ML-driven scoring.
• Experience taking a prototype to a reliable, maintainable production solution.
• Working knowledge of distributed systems, APIs, cloud-native development, and data or graph systems.
• Strong Python, and/or Java, Go, or TypeScript.
• Interest in security problems—vulnerability management, identity security, threat detection, or risk prioritization.
• Experience with AI-assisted development tools and coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or Windsurf is a plus.
• Experience with AI evaluation, safety, or guardrails is a plus.

• 3+ years of software engineering experience, or equivalent practical experience.

• Modern AI experience: LLMs, RAG, embeddings, vector search, agentic workflows, model evaluation, or AI observability.

jobs.title: Patient Care Coordinator, CARDIO4Cities Brunei (Contract role)
jobs.description:
About the Role

Role Type: Full-Time
Reporting To: Nurse-in-Charge
Location: On-site at designated health centers within Brunei-Muara District, Brunei Darussalam
Project: CARDIO4Cities Brunei

Job Summary:

The Patient Care Coordinator will support the implementation of the CARDIO4Cities initiative across its various workstreams. Responsibilities will include patient engagement and outreach activities—such as re-engaging patients with chronic diseases who have missed or are overdue for follow-up care—as well as administrative, coordination, and data management support for other initiative activities as required.

This is a strictly non-clinical role. The successful candidate will be responsible for contacting patients using approved communication scripts, coordinating follow-up appointments with the nursing team, maintaining accurate records of outreach activities, and escalating any clinical concerns to the appropriate healthcare team.

The role requires a warm and respectful approach when communicating with patients, as well as strong attention to detail when maintaining patient-related administrative information.

Key Responsibilities

1. Patient Re-engagement and Outreach

• Contact patients who have missed or are overdue for chronic disease follow-up appointments through approved phone calls or messaging channels.

• Use approved communication scripts and follow established procedures when communicating with patients.

• Encourage patients to return for their scheduled follow-up care in a warm, respectful, and non-judgmental manner.

• Record patient responses and outreach outcomes accurately and promptly.

• Follow up with patients as required in accordance with the established outreach process.

2. Appointment and Care Coordination

• Work closely with the nursing team to coordinate follow-up appointments for patients who agree to return for care.

• Assist with scheduling relevant investigations and/or follow-up appointments as directed by the nursing team.

• Ensure appointment information and patient responses are accurately recorded in the relevant system or database.

• Support the nursing team with administrative coordination related to patient re-engagement activities.

3. Non-Clinical Role Boundaries and Escalation

• Adhere strictly to the boundaries of a non-clinical role.

• Do not provide medical advice, clinical recommendations, diagnosis, or treatment guidance to patients.

• Follow applicable procedures regarding access to and handling patient information. The patient care coordinator must not access confidential medical records, except where access to specific administrative information (such as appointment details) is expressly authorized in writing by the nurse-in-charge and is strictly necessary to perform the duties of the role.

• Recognize and promptly escalate any clinical concerns, urgent symptoms, or other red flags reported by patients to the nursing team in accordance with established protocols to ensure timely clinical intervention.

• Refer patients to the appropriate healthcare professional whenever a matter falls outside the scope of the role.

4. Database and Activity Management

• Maintain accurate and up-to-date records relating to patient outreach and follow-up activities.

• Record call and messaging outcomes, patient responses, appointment arrangements, and other relevant activity accurately.

• Identify and report inconsistencies or missing information in the relevant database or records to the nursing team for resolution.

• Maintain proper documentation to support accurate tracking of patient re-engagement activities and outcomes.

• Handle all patient-related information securely and in accordance with applicable policies and procedures.

Required skills and qualifications

1. Communication and Patient Engagement

• Strong interpersonal skills, with the ability to communicate respectfully and effectively with patients, colleagues, and healthcare teams.

• Warm, empathetic, and non-judgmental telephone manners.

• Good listening and problem-solving skills.

• Ability to communicate sensitive matters professionally and respectfully.

• Fluent in spoken and written Bahasa Melayu and English.

2. Computer and Data Skills

• High level of computer and data literacy, with confidence in using common workplace software to organize, update, and secure patient records.

• Strong working knowledge of Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets, including advanced spreadsheet functions, meticulous data logging, activity tracking, and reporting.

• Strong attention to detail when entering, updating, and checking information.

• Ability to maintain organized and accurate records.

3. Compliance and Professional Conduct

• Demonstrates a strong understanding of confidentiality and the importance of protecting patient information.

• Able to follow Ministry of Health policies, applicable data protection requirements, and relevant workplace procedures.

• Maintains a high level of professionalism, integrity, and respect when dealing with patients and healthcare professionals.

• Able to work independently while also working effectively as part of a healthcare team.

4. Performance and Accountability

• Able to meet agreed weekly performance targets for the number of patients successfully contacted and logged.

• Consistently records outreach activities and outcomes accurately and within the required timeframe.

• Demonstrates reliability, organization, and accountability in completing assigned tasks.

Why Join Us?

• Contribute to the implementation of CARDIO4Cities in Brunei Darussalam, a population health initiative focused on improving cardiovascular health.

• Play a direct role in helping patients return to appropriate follow-up care and supporting better management of chronic disease.

• Work alongside healthcare professionals and contribute to a meaningful health initiative involving local and international partners.

• Gain practical experience in patient engagement, healthcare coordination, data management, and population health.

Additional Context:

Despite being largely preventable, cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the world’s leading cause of death, causing significant strain on countries’ health systems and economies, especially in cities, where most of the global population lives. Each year, more than 20 million people die from CVD, of which 75% occur in low- and middle-income countries, many prematurely before the age of 60. Meanwhile, high-income countries are experiencing a resurgence of CVD, disproportionately so in underserved populations.

By 2050, 70% of the world’s population will be urban, and cities will face a growing burden of CVD, compounded by rising inequities linked to social, economic, and environmental determinants of health, along with limited healthcare infrastructure and a shortage of skilled health workers. This calls for reimagining the way we address CV health, adopting a new approach that addresses both the medical and social determinants driving CVD, and cities are the best places to start.

In response, the Novartis Foundation established the CARDIO4Cities initiative. CARDIO4Cities consists of six interdependent pillars to accelerate and improve access to quality CV health and care, creating more livable, heart-healthy cities. The six pillars of CARDIO are quality of care, early access, policy reform, data and digital, intersectoral collaboration, and local ownership. The approach provides a framework to rapidly reduce overall CV risk in urban populations that is science-backed and offers concrete guidance on how to design and implement city-wide CV health interventions that are tailored to local priorities and needs.

CARDIO4Cities has already reached over 40 million people, demonstrating the scalability of the approach. Validated in three pioneering cities—São Paulo (Brazil), Dakar (Senegal), and Ulaanbaatar (Mongolia)—the CARDIO4Cities initiative has demonstrated strong results, including:

• Rapid improvement in heart health: In pioneering cities, control rates for blood pressure increased 3-6x within 1 year of implementation1, translating into an estimated reduction in strokes and heart attacks of 12% respectively 13%.

• Proven cost-effectiveness: In pioneering cities, the initiative had a 76% lower cost per QALY gained compared to costing benchmark2 and is determined to be cost-effective under WHO-CHOICE3. Accelerated detection and management of CV risk: Using a data-driven approach, CARDIO4Cities has proven successful in optimizing diagnosis of CV risk factors within and outside health facilities and improving risk factor management by simplifying and streamlining guidelines and translating them into clinical decision support tools for health providers (incl. team-based care).

jobs.title: Product Designer, Youth
jobs.description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. The Youth team is focused on making AI safe, useful, and empowering for young people.

Our work spans foundational protections—including age assurance and always-on safety—as well as new learning and education experiences. We’re also exploring how OpenAI’s technology can support K–12 schools, educators, classrooms, and collaborative learning.

About the Role

We’re looking for a staff-level product designer to shape how young people safely engage with AI and help define OpenAI’s emerging education experiences. You’ll work across immediate product needs and ambitious zero-to-one opportunities, from age-appropriate safety systems to tools for learning and group work.

A high craft bar is imperative. You’ll be expected to pair exceptional interaction and visual design with deep product thinking—turning complex questions around safety, learning, and institutional needs into experiences that feel clear, trustworthy, and engaging.

This is a highly generative role for someone who can move from early exploration to concrete, high-fidelity product direction. You’ll partner closely with product, engineering, research, safety, policy, and design to establish durable patterns for a space that is still being defined.

This role is based in our San Francisco HQ. We offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role you will:

 - Establish an exceptionally high standard for craft across OpenAI’s youth and education experiences.

 - Lead end-to-end design for products that help young people use AI safely, confidently, and productively.

 - Design clear, age-appropriate experiences for safety, age assurance, and other sensitive or high-trust interactions.

 - Shape zero-to-one K–12 experiences spanning school districts, educators, classrooms, collaborative work, and builder-style workflows.

 - Turn emerging ideas into compelling concepts, prototypes, and high-fidelity product experiences that teams can evaluate and build.

 - Partner with research, engineering, product, safety, policy, and design to balance user needs, technical capabilities, and responsible deployment.

 - Conduct and apply research with relevant users and partners to understand the needs of young people, educators, and institutions.

 - Develop reusable patterns and principles that create coherence across youth and education products as the area grows.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Bring exceptional interaction and visual design craft and are motivated to raise the quality of design across OpenAI.

 - Are a highly generative designer who explores broadly, iterates deeply, and turns ideas into concrete, polished product direction.

 - Pair strong craft with deep product and systems thinking.

 - Have led substantial, ambiguous, or zero-to-one product areas and can help shape both vision and execution.

 - Can design thoughtful experiences for sensitive, high-trust, or safety-critical contexts.

 - Understand how to create products that are engaging and intuitive without compromising safety or clarity.

 - Can navigate the needs of multiple audiences, including young people, educators, administrators, and institutional partners.

 - Communicate clearly, build alignment across disciplines, and remain hands-on throughout the product-development process.

 - Are energized by the opportunity to define how AI can support learning while serving young people responsibly.

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.

The job entails becoming a SME in all warehouse processes and being able to take on special projects, suggest CIPs to increase productivity and efficiency as well as coordinating with cross-functional teams.

Essential Job Duties

This position will fulfill the following roles (If applicable to site):

• Shipping: Verifies, checks, validates, and receives the shipments incoming and outgoing material to make sure, labels, packing slips, BOL’s other shipping documents and serial cans are done, attached and processed according to work instructions
• Receiving: Receiving materials, physically and systemically, to be used in production operations and engineering projects.
• Parts Put-away: Physically and systemically moving approved Production materials from IQC staging areas into market storage locations. (Totes and Bulk)
• Storage Market (SMKT, KMKT, MMKT, SVKT, etc.):Point-of-use parts replenishment, for designated production lines.Parts Replenishment: Point-of-use parts replenishment for designated production lines. • Inventory Control: Understand full flow of the material within stockroom locations. Participate in Cycle Count, Physical Inventories, and reconciliation activities in coordination with Inventory analyst, conduct material audits and parts verification and evaluate bin capacity and consolidations to increase storage capacity. Maintain various SOX compliance audit records and suggest CIPs to improve warehouse efficiency.

• Ensure the business unit is always audit ready.

• Maintain warehouse safety and housekeeping in accordance with 5S principles.
• Achieve all warehouse-related tasks certifications.
• Communicating verbally and via email the status of material movements and transactions to appropriate internal customers.
• Actively participate in the Continuous Improvement program, including the creation and implementation of small-scale improvements.
• Able to locate and count parts accurately (using cycle-count documents), execute required WMS data input and accurately complete required documentation.

• Ability to obtain certification across all core curriculums.

• Minimum 1 year of related experience
• Ability to adhere to attendance, safety, quality, and performance guidelines.
• Knowledge of Agile and SAP.
• Experience with computer systems (MS Office, Agile, WMS) is preferred.
• Inventory control experience (cycle counting, physical inventories).

jobs.title: W Series Vehicle Scheduler
jobs.description:
About Varda

Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules. Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.

From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.

Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.

Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.

Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.

About This Role

As a W-Series Vehicle Scheduler, you will develop, analyze, and maintain integrated vehicle schedules for Varda Space's growing fleet as the company scales its product lines toward more advanced mission objectives and an increasing operational cadence. Reporting directly to the VP, W-Series Vehicles, you will identify critical path drivers across subsystems engineering, systems integration and test, supply chain, and production, supporting Varda's target of 12+ vehicles per year. You will own baseline schedule development for vehicle block upgrades and sustain recurring reentry vehicle schedules.

Responsibilities

• Develop, maintain, and analyze integrated master schedules (IMS) in Microsoft Project or equivalent tooling across the W-Series Vehicle fleet

• Partner with Vehicle Systems, Integration and Test leadership, and engineering task leads to translate scope into executable plans aligned with budget and technical objectives

• Identify critical path, near-critical activities, and key schedule drivers to support informed decision-making

• Lead weekly schedule updates, status collection, and forecast adjustments; clearly communicate risks, impacts, and recovery options

• Support baseline development, re-baselining efforts, engineering change cut-ins, and change management activities throughout the program lifecycle

• Assist the VP, W-Series Vehicles and Finance with monthly earned value metrics, including mission-related spend and non-recurring and recurring engineering labor

• Perform schedule quality checks and health assessments in accordance with industry best practices and Varda standards

• Drive scheduling process improvements through standardization, automation, and tool enhancements

• Ensure schedules are defensible, audit-ready, and aligned with leadership expectations

• Support program reviews and provide scheduling expertise to facilitate decision-making

Basic Qualifications

• B.S. or M.S. with emphasis in Project Management or related field

• 5–10+ years of experience in mission, space vehicle, or production scheduling

• Expertise in schedule management tools, including MS Project and Smartsheet

• Proficiency in manufacturing resource planning (MRP) tools

• Strong communication and collaboration skills in a cross-functional environment

Preferred Skills and Experience

• Experience in a fast-paced aerospace or technology startup environment

• Background in space or aviation hardware production

• Familiarity with streamlined earned value management methods and tools

Pay Range

• This role is on-site in El Segundo, CA

• Leveling and base salary is determined by job-related skills, education level, experience level, and job performance

• You will be eligible for incentives in the form of stock options and/or long-term cash awards

Benefits

Consider your benefits covered for launch. At Varda, we invest in benefits and perks that support your health, financial well-being, and life beyond work. Benefits vary by position, with packages designed specifically for our regular full-time employees and interns.

Regular Full-Time Positions:

• 100% company-paid Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance plans for employees and dependents with FSA and employer-matched HSA options

• Voluntary accident, hospital, critical illness, and pet insurance

• $120/month wellness reimbursement for gym and fitness expenses

• 12 weeks of parental leave (with supplemental disability leave for CA mothers)

• Family building, pregnancy, parenting and menopause benefits via Maven Clinic

• Sponsored One Medical memberships for employees and their dependents

Financial & Retirement

jobs.title: Electrician, Medium Voltage (Starship)
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

ELECTRICIAN, MEDIUM VOLTAGE (STARSHIP)

As a Medium Voltage Electrician, you will support the installation, inspection, testing, maintenance, and repair of electrical equipment in substations and power grid facilities to ensure safe, reliable power delivery. This role focuses on basic tasks under direct supervision, working with energized equipment up to 260 volts initially, progressing to higher voltages (above 750 volts) after training. You will assist higher-classified personnel in high- and medium-voltage environments, following strict safety standards. This position combines core responsibilities from substation technician and station electrician roles, emphasizing hands-on learning and team collaboration.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Assist in installing, inspecting, maintaining, and repairing substation equipment, including breakers, transformers, switches, relays, buswork, control systems, and batteries.

• Perform basic routine maintenance on high- and medium-voltage electrical systems, such as cleaning, lubrication, and visual inspections (e.g., checking oil levels, lights, heaters, and connections).

• Conduct entry-level electrical testing, including using voltmeters, ohmmeters, ammeters, insulation meggers, and assisting with insulation resistance, relay, transformer, and circuit breaker tests.

• Read and interpret basic electrical drawings, one-line diagrams, schematics, wiring diagrams, and work orders with guidance.

• Troubleshoot simple electrical, mechanical, and control system issues under supervision.

• Follow lockout/tagout (LOTO), grounding, clearance procedures, and safety protocols (e.g., PPE, emergency rescue techniques like steel/aerial lift rescue).

• Assist in station switching, de-energizing equipment, placing grounds, and coordinating with operators, engineers, and utility crews during outages or Operations.

• Help with physical tasks: digging/backfilling trenches, installing conduit/pipe/cable/wire, uncrating materials, painting structures, climbing ladders/structures (up to 50+ ft), and operating hand/power tools, portable generators, blowers, and pumps.

• Support emergency responses to outages, faults, and call-outs for prompt service restoration.

• Document work performed, test results, and observations accurately; maintain records and prepare basic reports.

• Replace simple components like lamps, switches, outlets, dry cells; assist with oil sampling/handling and signal/communication systems.

• Participate in training sessions, assist in training others, and become familiar with company safety rules, First Aid.

• Operate company vehicles and specialized equipment; inspect and store personal protective equipment (PPE).

• Perform similar or less skilled incidental duties as assigned.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• High school diploma or equivalency certificate.

• 3+ years of experience working as a licensed electrician.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• Associate degree in electrical, mechanical, industrial maintenance technology.

• Basic understanding of electrical principles (AC/DC circuits, safety standards).

• Ability to read basic prints/drawings and use common test tools.

• Proficiency with hand/power tools and physical tasks (lifting 50+ lbs, working at heights/confined spaces, outdoors in all weather).

• Strong safety focus, attention to detail, and ability to work independently or in teams.

• Knowledge of print reading for drawings, manuals, and one-lines.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

• Schedule varies depending on site operational needs and flexibility required regarding frequent overtime/weekend support.

• Ability to work in an environment requiring exposure to fumes, odors, and noise.

• Ability to rapidly change roles/responsibilities while working in a high-paced, challenging work environment.

• Stand: Up to 6 hours per day.

• Sit: Up to 3 hours per day.

• Push/Pull: Up to 75lbs. (unassisted) 1-2 hours per day.

• Overhead reach: Up to 3 hours per day.

• Walk: Up to 3 hours per day.

• Lift/Carry: Up to 50lbs. (unassisted) 1-2 hours per day.

• Climb (ladder/stairs): Up to 3 hours per day.

• Kneel/Crouch: Up to 3 hours per day.

• Upper body twist: Up to 6 hours per day.

• Ability to work in temperatures over 80 degrees up to 3 hours per day.

• Candidate must be capable of safely working at heights (up to 500ft), in confined spaces, working with high voltage, and performing the physical requirements of the job listed in the job description. Candidate may be required to complete a pre-employment questionnaire and/or physical to confirm these capabilities, which may include a medical history review.

Real-world data is the competitive edge in AI.

HumanSignal is a human data partner for companies building AI models and products. Our customers ship better AI, faster, because we partner with their researchers from real-world data creation to annotation to delivery.

We design and create datasets from scratch, recruit and manage the domain experts who evaluate model output, and run everything through our own platform, Label Studio, the open-source standard for data labeling and evaluation, used by over 1 million practitioners worldwide.

We specialize in the operationally complex: real-world data collection, multimodal pipelines, and multi-step workflows. Advanced ML and AI teams use our enterprise platform to run their own data factories, and our services team to extend their reach where in-house capacity runs out.

If you want to do work that materially shapes how the next generation of AI products gets built, we'd love to talk.

Casting & Talent Coordinator

HumanSignal operates a production studio in Columbus where local performers record on-camera sessions used to train AI systems. We’re looking for a part-time Casting & Talent Coordinator to build and manage a strong, reliable pipeline of local performers. You'll be representing this work to a performing arts community that has questions about AI, so comfort having that conversation directly matters.

• Recruit professional actors, voice actors, aspiring performers, and people with strong natural on-camera presence through in-person and online outreach.

• You have experience in casting, talent booking, recruiting, theater or improv production, community outreach, or a related field, or you have strong relationships across Columbus’s performing arts community.

• You are comfortable approaching new people, building trust, and representing HumanSignal professionally in creative communities.

• You can recognize strong on-camera presence and potential, make sound screening recommendations, and explain your reasoning clearly.

• You know how to help candidates feel prepared and confident without over-coaching them.

• You are resourceful and persistent. When one recruiting channel isn’t working, you test new messages, venues, partnerships, or sources.

• You are organized and can maintain accurate records across multiple recruiting channels and stages of the candidate pipeline.

• You communicate clearly and can discuss the nature of AI-related work transparently and respectfully, including responding thoughtfully to questions or concerns.

Details

jobs.title: Launch and Recovery Engineering Manager

About Varda

Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules. Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.

From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.

Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.

Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.

Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.

About This Role

As a Launch & Recovery Engineering Manager you will have the primary responsibility for owning and defining the launch vehicle mechanical and electrical interface and capsule recovery operations for Varda Space Vehicles as the company innovates and scales its product lines for more advanced mission objectives along with a higher operational cadence. The role is responsible for launch vehicle and recovery requirements definition for Varda Space Vehicles, delivery of all technical and regulatory contract deliverables to the launch provider per the Launch Services Agreement (LSA), definition of launch vehicle ICD with the launch provider, and management and execution of launch site I&T and capsule recovery procedures. This role will report directly to the VP, W-Series Vehicles within Vehicle Systems, Integration and Test engineering interfacing with all subsystem engineering departments, mission operations engineers as well as senior leadership.

This is a people management role with direct reports. The Launch & Recovery Engineering Manager will be responsible for building and leading a team of engineers, with expectations that include:

• Directly managing, mentoring, and developing a team of launch and recovery engineers

• Setting individual goals, conducting performance reviews, and supporting career growth for direct reports

• Hiring and onboarding new team members as the launch cadence scales to 12+ vehicles per year

• Delegating and prioritizing work across the team to meet mission milestones and LSA commitments

• Fostering a collaborative, high-performance team culture aligned with Varda's mission and values

• Coordinating cross-functionally with subsystem leads, mission operations, and senior leadership on behalf of the team

Responsibilities

• Responsible for definition of Launch Vehicle Interface technical and regulatory requirements for Varda Space Industries vehicles through early mission lifecycle reviews (i.e. Design Criteria, Preliminary Design, Critical Design) leading to definition and execution of all contracted Launch Service Agreements (LSA)

• Serves as primary responsible engineer for all technical and regulatory contract deliverables through execution of an LSA from contract effective date to include mission integration, dynamics model, mass properties, mechanical & electrical interface specifications, launch vehicle separation configuration & analysis, Range Safety, FAA/FCC licensing, hazardous procedures, launch site campaign planning and integration and test procedure definition

• Chairs regular meetings (i.e. biweekly) with Launch Provider to ensure all LSA technical and regulatory deliverables are meeting their contractual commitments, coordinating any schedule impacts or trades with the VP, W-Series Vehicles

• Co-chairs specific anomaly investigations and corrective action with mission assurance that directly impact LSA contract technical deliverables to include the critical environmental test report

• Manages the execution of all launch site Integration and Test procedures for each Varda Space mission, leading a cross-disciplinary team to include parallel processing of multiple vehicles

• Develops capsule recovery concept of operations, plans and procedures, directly participating in capsule recovery operations at the Australian Koonibba test range and future recovery sites

• Works with executive management to scale launch and recovery planning and execution for an expected cadence of 12+ vehicles per year, which includes implementation of a team structure with standardization of interfaces and contract deliverables for multiple launch providers

• Performs detailed system-level technical and cost trade studies for additional launch vehicles as part of achieving an increased reentry vehicle operational cadence

Basic Qualifications

• B.S. degree in engineering, physics, or related field and (typically 5–10+ years) of experience in systems, integration, and/or test

• Prior experience in a formal or informal people management or technical leadership role, with demonstrated ability to lead, mentor, and develop engineers

• Comprehensive understanding of satellite systems engineering, including all satellite subsystems

• Thorough knowledge of launch vehicle mechanical and electrical engineering interface technical specifications

• Strong familiarity with AFSPCMAN 91-710 requirements to include propulsion, structures, avionics, mechanisms, and software

• Ability to solve complex problems autonomously as an individual contributor or as a member of an integrated team

• Proven track record in a technical leadership role for a launch vehicle or satellite program

• Strong teamwork, communication, and problem-solving skills in a collaborative environment

• Demonstrated success working on complex technical programs, preferably within aerospace or related industries

• First principles thinking and broad technical fluency across relevant fields (electrical, mechanical, software, etc.)

• Hands-on background building and testing satellites or operating them in a space environment

Preferred Skills and Experience

• M.S. degree in engineering, physics, or related field is preferred

• Active Top Secret/SCI eligible clearance is strongly preferred

• Proficiency in one or more general-purpose programming languages, such as C++ or Python

• Familiarity with aerospace hardware development practices (e.g., qualification testing, design for typical space environments, cleanliness standards, etc.)

• Background testing spacecraft or launch vehicle flight hardware, particularly launch separation systems

• Exposure to a production or high-cadence manufacturing environment

• Proficiency in Unigraphics NX or similar CAD software

Pay Range

Benefits

jobs.title: AI Red Teamer (LLM Generalist)
jobs.description:
AI RED TEAMER (LLM GENERALIST)

Location: Seattle, WA (candidates must reside in the Seattle metro area or be willing to relocate prior to start)
Type: Contract, 40 hours per week


ABOUT THE ROLE

As an AI Red Teamer, you will stress-test large language models by intentionally trying to break them. Rather than checking whether an answer is correct, you will design creative, adversarial prompts that expose vulnerabilities: unsafe content, bias, broken guardrails, hallucinations, prompt injection weaknesses, and unexpected behaviors. Your work directly supports AI safety and model robustness for leading research labs.

This is a generalist red teaming role. You will probe models across the full spectrum of risk categories, including content safety, CBRN (chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear), cybersecurity, persuasion and influence operations, child safety, self-harm, over-companionship, and regulatory compliance. Red teaming may span text, image, voice, and agentic model capabilities depending on project needs.

This role requires creativity, curiosity, and an ability to think like an adversary while operating with strong ethical judgment.


DAY-TO-DAY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Craft creative prompts and multi-turn scenarios to stress-test AI guardrails across diverse risk categories

 - Discover ways around safety filters, restrictions, and defenses using jailbreak, evasion, and prompt injection techniques

 - Explore edge cases to provoke disallowed, harmful, or incorrect outputs

 - Evaluate and score model responses against structured harm taxonomies and severity rubrics

 - Document experiments clearly, including what you tried, why you tried it, and what it revealed

 - Review and refine adversarial prompts generated by other team members

 - Contribute to harm taxonomy development, calibration exercises, and inter-rater reliability work

 - Collaborate with engineers, data scientists, and researchers to share findings and strengthen defenses

 - Work with potentially disturbing content on a regular basis (see Content Warning below)

 - Stay current on jailbreaks, attack methods, and evolving model behaviors


DESIRED CAPABILITIES

Core

 - Strong hands-on experience using multiple LLMs (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, open-source models, etc.)

 - Intuition for crafting adversarial prompts; familiarity with jailbreak or evasion techniques is a strong plus

 - Creative, adversarial problem-solving skills

 - Clear and thoughtful written communication

 - Strong ethical judgment and the ability to separate adversarial thinking from personal values

 - Self-directed, collaborative, and comfortable in feedback-heavy environments

 - Curiosity, persistence, and comfort with frequent failure in experimentation

Nice to Have

 - Familiarity with Python or other scripting languages

 - Experience working with LLM APIs or evaluation tooling

 - Comfort with structured data annotation and rubric-based scoring

 - Prior work in trust and safety, content moderation, QA, or security research

 - Subject matter expertise in any high-risk domain (cybersecurity, chemistry, biology, medicine, law, finance, etc.)


YOU WILL THRIVE HERE IF

 - You treat every model response as a hypothesis to challenge

 - You can switch between creative free-association and rigorous documentation in the same session

 - You go deep into unusual interests (fandoms, niche internet cultures, gaming exploits, Wikipedia rabbit holes, etc.)

 - You come from a creative background: writing, visual art, improv, puzzle design, or similar

 - You are energized by finding the thing nobody else thought to try

 - You are genuinely passionate about AI and follow the space closely


CONTENT WARNING

This role involves regular and deliberate exposure to harmful content. You will encounter and intentionally generate content involving violence, self-harm, hate speech, sexually explicit material, child safety scenarios, and other categories of harmful output as part of structured adversarial testing. Candidates must be able to engage with this material professionally and sustainably. Support resources are available.


ABOUT HANDSHAKE AI

Handshake AI partners with leading AI research labs to make models safer and more robust. Our red teaming operations help identify vulnerabilities before they reach users, contributing directly to the responsible development of frontier AI systems.

jobs.title: Director, Product Management
jobs.description:
About Understood

Understood is a nonprofit focused on shaping the world for difference. We raise awareness of the challenges and strengths of people who learn and think differently. Our resources help people navigate challenges, gain confidence, and find support and community so they can thrive.

Having a shared commitment to our values is a key factor in any hire we make. We have five core values:

• Continuously learn.

• Act with intention.

• Champion difference.

• Inspire change.

• Grow together.

Come be part of an organization with an entrepreneurial spirit that’s helping to shape the world for difference. Together, we can build a world where everyone can reach their full potential.

To learn more about Understood, please visit: www.understood.org.

Who you are

To advance Understood’s mission and to further our impact, we’re hiring a Director of Product Management, reporting to our VP Product.

Millions of people, who navigate neurodivergence or support someone who does, come to Understood.org to find accessible and trustworthy resources grounded in clinical expertise and evidence.

We are seeking a product leader to set the product direction for how artificial intelligence intersects with our users' everyday lives and lead the strategy, definition, and execution of our AI-based consumer products. This is a high-impact, player-coach role that combines hands-on product leadership with leading and developing other product managers (PMs). You will influence the organization through product strategy leadership, deep technical fluency, and a strong focus on the consumer.

You have a track record of leveraging AI to drive positive consumer and business outcomes, managing PMs and partnering cross-functionally to iteratively deliver effective and engaging product experiences.

This is a hybrid role that requires a minimum of three (3) days a week in our NYC office, with a focus on Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday. We are a Mac-based environment, and team members are provided a Mac laptop for their work.

What you’ll do

• Drive the AI-enabled product vision: Define and own the strategy and roadmap for our AI-enabled platform that powers a portfolio of personalized consumer solutions, making platform-level tradeoffs based on the needs of the broader portfolio. Additionally, own both the strategy and execution of our flagship consumer-facing AI-chat. Work closely with internal and external subject matter experts to identify and execute on opportunities where machine learning and generative AI can uniquely solve user problems or create new behaviors.

• Lead the PM team: Inspire and lead a team of product managers to identify, plan, and deliver high-impact initiatives from zero to one and one and through product-market fit (PMF), regardless of how deeply they leverage AI. Own team priorities and make decisions about talent, resourcing, and how work is allocated across the team.

• Navigate AI UX challenges: Design products that effectively handle the non-deterministic nature of AI. Champion solutions for latency, model hallucinations, trust, and privacy while maintaining a frictionless consumer experience. Push the boundaries of what is feasible while managing tradeoffs between model size, cost, and speed, while ensuring we use AI safely and responsibly.

• Establish data flywheels: Design intuitive mechanisms for continuous model improvement, ensuring that user interactions create feedback loops that make the product smarter over time.

• Build strong cross-functional partnerships with Design, UX Research, Engineering, Subject Matter Experts (e.g., AI researchers, data scientists, clinical experts), Marketing, and Content teams. Make tradeoffs across teams and initiatives when priorities compete.

• Define and measure success: Refine and own KPIs that evaluate both the underlying AI performance (accuracy, speed) and the consumer outcome (retention, engagement, and other measures of user value). Use data and insights to shape product strategy, priorities, and investment decisions.

• Be an advocate for our product, team, and values

Minimum qualifications

In this role, you bring leadership experience and the ability to set direction across a capability. You also own team-level priorities, manage multiple direct reports, including hiring and resourcing decisions, own the team budget, and communicate directly with the leadership and executive leadership teams.

We don't expect a perfect match across every category. What matters is relevant experience, genuine interest in the work, and a mindset for growth.

Leadership and people

• Experience: 10+ years of product management experience in consumer-facing technology, including 3+ years leading a team or area of the business in a fast-moving or complex environment. You have owned team-level priorities and delivered results that have had an impact across the organization.

• People leadership and development: You have 3+ years of experience managing product managers and managing multiple direct reports. You make decisions on hiring, team structure, and resourcing for the team. You coach and develop people. You build a culture where people feel they belong, stay engaged, and hold themselves accountable. You keep the team motivated through change and resistance.

• Stakeholder and cross-functional partnership: You work effectively with leaders in other functions, senior leaders, and direct reports. You make tradeoffs across teams when priorities compete. You build strong working relationships up, down, and across the organization, including in a hybrid setting.

Strategy, execution, and data

• Domain expertise: You have deep expertise in consumer product management, including experience building and shipping AI/ML-driven consumer products. You have a track record of leveraging AI to drive positive consumer and business outcomes and creating intuitive consumer experiences from complex technology.

• Strategic thinking and execution: You turn company strategy, user needs, and emerging technology into clear product plans and priorities. You balance long-term thinking with hands-on execution and adjust the plan when conditions change.

• Project management: You plan and run multiple product initiatives across the team and functions. You set clear milestones, manage risk and dependencies, and keep the team on track to deliver.

• Data and analytics: You develop insights to shape product strategy and priorities. You decide what data and success measures are needed. You use analysis to test ideas, evaluate outcomes, and make better product decisions.

Communication, collaboration, and technology fluency

• Communication: You communicate clearly and confidently with leadership and executive leadership teams, peer leaders, direct reports, and external partners. You translate complex AI concepts for technical and non-technical audiences, adapt your message to the audience, and build trust through consistent, inclusive communication.

• Collaboration and ways of working: You work collaboratively without letting hierarchy or personal credit drive decisions. You work with integrity, emotional awareness, and resilience through change. You advocate for users, employees, and the organization in decision-making.

• AI fluency: You have strong technical fluency in machine learning and generative AI, including the concepts and considerations required to build and scale AI-enabled consumer products safely and responsibly. You use AI tools to improve the team’s output, speed, or decisions and set expectations for how the team uses them responsibly.

Mission alignment

• You are committed to Understood’s mission and to creating accessible, trustworthy products for people who learn and think differently.

Nice-to-haves

• Experience in health tech, behavioral health, wellbeing or education products

• Experience using modern AI frameworks and APIs to explore and test product concepts.

The base salary range for this role is $235,000 - $250,000, depending on years of experience and qualifications. We offer a comprehensive benefits package that supports wellness for our team members and their families. You can learn more about our benefits and offerings.

Understood.org does not sponsor applicants for work visas or legal permanent residence, including providing assistance with STEM OPT extensions.

Commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion

Understood encourages individuals of all learning styles and ethnic, racial, and socioeconomic backgrounds, including those whose life experiences may include the challenge of access due to a disability, to apply for this position. We are committed to maximizing the diversity of our organization, as we want to engage all those who can contribute to supporting this work.

Understood is an equal opportunity employer and considers all applications without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, national origin, ancestry, age, alienage or citizenship status, marital or familial status, domestic partnership status, caregiver status, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity or expression, change of sex or transgender status, genetic information, medical condition, pregnancy, childbirth or related medical conditions, physical or mental disability (where the applicant or employee is qualified to perform the essential functions of the job with or without reasonable accommodation), any protected military or veteran status, or status as a victim of domestic or dating violence, sexual assault or offense, stalking, or any other characteristics protected by federal, state, or local law or that of persons with whom that individual associates, or any other legally protected characteristics.

For additional information on learning and thinking differences, including ADD/ADHD, dyslexia, dyscalculia, dysgraphia, dyspraxia, executive function challenges, nonverbal learning disabilities, processing issues, and more, please visit www.understood.org.
