jobs.title: Head of Legal
jobs.description:
ABOUT TIN CAN

Tin Can is building a safer, simpler way for kids to connect, without smartphones. We’re creating screen-free, delightful devices and services that let families call the people who matter most, free from the noise of today’s digital world.

We’re building a bold, authentic, nostalgic, and kinda quirky brand that resonates with folks who want something simpler & better for their kids than the tech-infused lives we’re currently living (and who have a sense of humor about it). As we gear up to scale to thousands of families, we’re ready to bring on a Head of Legal to help make it happen.




THE ROLE

If we get something wrong in the fine print (a compliance gap on a new device, a contract that leaves us exposed, a regulatory question we didn’t see coming), it doesn’t stay a legal problem for long. It becomes a broken promise to the families who trusted us with their kids’ first phone. We’re looking for a Head of Legal to make sure that never happens: our senior-most in-house legal mind, and the first full-time legal hire embedded in the day-to-day of the company.

You’ll build on the foundation our fractional General Counsel has laid, partnering directly with our leadership team on the legal questions of building and selling physical, connected products, including FCC and telecom regulation, product compliance, children’s privacy, and international expansion. This isn’t a role for someone who wants to immediately manage a team of lawyers or delegate work away: you’re senior enough to own the strategic picture, but still hands-on yourself, building out the function, and a team if and when you decide we need one, as we scale.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

•      Guide compliance for every physical, connected product we sell to families, including internationally, and as we expand beyond a single device into new products and accessories, help build the compliance playbook for each new thing we launch

•      Own our compliance with privacy laws, including COPPA and the growing set of state and international equivalents, as the person ultimately responsible for how we collect, use, and protect our customers’ data

•      Support our go-to-market efforts as we expand into new countries, advising on the legal and regulatory considerations of entering new markets, from entity formation to product compliance to commercial terms

•      Review and advise on our direct-to-consumer marketing, advertising claims, promotions, and privacy considerations as a lifestyle brand marketed to parents

•      Draft, review, and redline our commercial agreements, including vendor and supplier contracts and partnership deals, deciding case by case what to handle yourself versus sending to outside counsel to balance efficiency, quality, and risk

•      Help figure out the legal and structural path for new product categories, partnerships, and business models we haven’t tried before, in real time rather than from an existing playbook

•     Own our regulatory and FCC posture; it’s a niche area, so get comfortable learning it fast and know when to bring in outside specialists to fill the gaps

•     Be the in-house resource for our People team on employment law, including offer letters, the handbook, and day-to-day HR compliance, so we’re not paying outside counsel for routine matters; HR doesn’t report to you, but you’ll be a key partner HR hire and know when something needs a specialist

•      Manage board mechanics, including consents, minutes, and equity grants, support capital raises, and keep our corporate governance, cap table, and equity matters clean and current

•      Know what to keep in-house and what to send out; build and manage budgets and relationships with outside counsel and subject-matter experts (regulatory, IP, international, litigation), and bring them in efficiently when needed




WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

•      10+ years of legal experience, including meaningful in-house time at a high growth technology or hardware company

•      Real entrepreneurial spirit and genuine willingness to do hands-on, detail-level work; you’re not too senior to redline an NDA yourself

•      A clear, plain-English communicator who can turn legal risk into a decision the team can act on

•      Familiarity with children’s privacy and data protection compliance (COPPA or international equivalents), or closely comparable consumer privacy work

•      Experience with physical product compliance, including international requirements, is a plus

•      Comfortable getting up to speed fast on FCC and telecom-adjacent regulatory work; expertise is a bonus, not a requirement

•      Experience supporting international expansion and go-to-market efforts

•      Familiarity with D2C consumer marketing legal considerations

•      Solid grounding in board governance work: consents, minutes, equity grants, and related corporate matters

•      Working knowledge of employment law fundamentals, enough to be a real resource to our HR team; deep specialization isn’t required

•      Fluency using AI as a multiplier across contract review, research, and drafting; this is how we work, not a nice-to-have

•      Low-ego and collaborative; you share credit and pitch in on problems that aren’t yours

•      Based in Seattle and ready to work from our office 4+ days per week; this isn’t a remote role




WHY JOIN TIN CAN

We’re building tech that protects childhood: We’re on a quest to give kids a more analog childhood: one with real conversations, real connection, and way less screen time. No doomscrolling, data mining, or dopamine traps, just a simpler, better way for kids to stay in touch. This is a rare opportunity to build something that truly matters.

You’ll own the whole legal picture, not just a slice of it: From FCC filings to the NDA on your desk, you’ll be our first full-time legal hire, building the function, and eventually a team, as you go.

Small, high-trust team: Every company says “team,” but at Tin Can it means something different. We’re a small, mission-driven group that genuinely has each other’s backs, professionally and personally. You’ll be joining a tight-knit crew where your ideas and instincts matter from day one.

Room to explore, not just execute: You’ll have the space to explore new ideas, challenge assumptions, and build a legal function that reflects our values of trust, simplicity, and care.

If you meet most of the qualifications above and you’re excited by the idea of protecting the promise we make to families, we encourage you to apply - even if you do not check every single box listed above.  We can’t wait to meet someone who’s ready to jump in, own the legal picture end to end, and help us grow.

jobs.title: Product Manager, Compute Operations
jobs.description:
ABOUT FLUIDSTACK

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it. 


We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!




HOW WE OPERATE

 - Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

 - Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

 - Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

 - Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

 - Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.




THE COMPUTE PRODUCTION TEAM

The Compute Production team builds the data foundations and internal products that let Fluidstack bring gigawatt-scale AI compute online and keep it running.

Examples of key problems the team is working on:

 - Build the ontology that models compute production end to end, from hardware and networks to the operational workflows that deliver clusters to customers

 - Turn fragmented operational data spread across tools, spreadsheets, and people's heads into a single source of truth engineers and operators can build against

 - Ship product surfaces that give compute production teams real leverage: fewer manual handoffs, faster diagnosis, clearer state of the fleet

 - Apply LLM-era tooling to operational workflows where structured data and automation can replace repetitive human effort


ROLE SCOPE

 - Own product direction for the team's ontology and data products serving compute production: the roadmap, the priorities, and the success metrics that justify them

 - Turn messy compute production domains into data models, specs, and product surfaces clear enough that engineers can ship against them without a second round of discovery

 - Drive technical tradeoffs with engineers and ship end to end, from problem definition through delivery

 - Run direct discovery with compute production stakeholders to understand their domain, then validate that what you built actually changes how they work

 - Define and track the metrics that prove the product is delivering real leverage, and cut or redirect work that isn't


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would. https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/fluidstack/05c2e69c-42f9-4fcb-9cf0-a467aaf98f1c

 - 3+ years of technical product management, ideally on data, platform, or ontology products

 - A track record of shipping products with measurable impact, and the numbers to show it

 - You can reason about system design and hold your own with engineers on technical tradeoffs, not just relay their conclusions

 - Strong written communication: crisp specs, and prioritization rationale sharp enough that stakeholders who disagree still understand why you chose what you chose

 - You're comfortable in ambiguity and know how to impose structure where none exists, turning an unmapped operational domain into a model others can build on

 - Bonus: exposure to compute or datacenter operations, infrastructure systems, or building LLM-powered applications



We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

Fluidstack is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Fluidstack will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records pursuant to applicable law.



You will receive a confirmation email once your application has successfully been accepted. If there is an error with your submission and you did not receive a confirmation email, please email careers@fluidstack.io with your resume/CV, the role you've applied for, and the date you submitted your application--  someone from our recruiting team will be in touch.

jobs.title: Senior Motion Designer
jobs.description:
About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About You and The Role

Zipline’s communications team shapes and shares the company’s story and impact. We develop and implement strategies and tactics to educate our target audiences about Zipline, tell stories that raise awareness about what we’re doing and the impact that we’re having, increase acceptance of and excitement for our system, and cultivate ambassadors. We are passionate storytellers and make complex topics simple and understandable.

Zipline is expanding in the U.S. and will be delivering food, medicine, retail items and more directly to people’s homes in many states over the next few years. We are seeking a Senior Motion Designer to bring Zipline’s products, operations, people, and impact to life through animation and motion graphics.
You will translate creative briefs, scripts, brand systems, and technical concepts into storyboards, style frames, animatics, and polished motion work. Your work will span social and brand video, product launches, explainers, events, web, and presentations. You will work closely with Communications, Brand, Social, Marketing, engineers, and operators, as well as a Video Producer, Cinematographer, and Editor. This is a hands-on role for a designer who combines strong visual fundamentals with animation craft and can make complex technology clear, accurate, and compelling.

What You'll Do

• Design and animate motion graphics for social and brand video, product launches, technical explainers, customer stories, events, web, and presentations.
• Translate briefs, scripts, static designs, and technical information into storyboards, style frames, motion studies, animatics, and final animation.
• Create clear visual explanations of Zipline’s products and operations using typography, maps, diagrams, data, product interfaces, callouts, and 2D and 3D animation.
• Develop titles, lower thirds, transitions, end cards, graphic packages, and other motion elements that integrate cleanly with live-action footage.
• Composite motion and visual effects into footage, including screen replacements, tracked graphics, masks, cleanup, and other shot-based work.
• Collaborate with the Editor on timing, pacing, integration, renders, revisions, and delivery of motion assets within finished video.
• Partner with the Video Producer to estimate effort, confirm requirements, plan reviews, and deliver work against production schedules.
• Work with brand designers and creative partners to apply Zipline’s visual identity consistently in motion across channels and formats.
• Collaborate with engineers, operators, and other subject-matter experts to represent products, interfaces, workflows, and operational details accurately.
• Build and maintain reusable templates, animation components, title systems, project files, and documentation that improve consistency and production efficiency.
• Adapt work across durations, aspect ratios, resolutions, placements, and regional versions while preserving visual quality and brand consistency.
• Maintain organized source files, linked assets, naming conventions, version history, render settings, and archives for efficient collaboration and reuse.

What You'll Bring

• 6+ years of professional motion design experience in an in-house creative team, agency, studio, production company, or similarly demanding environment.
• A strong reel and portfolio demonstrating motion craft, design judgment, visual storytelling, and range across 2D and 3D work, with your role identified for each project.
• Expert proficiency in Adobe After Effects and strong working proficiency in Illustrator, Photoshop, and Figma.
• Professional experience with Cinema 4D, Blender, or another 3D package, including animation, lighting, rendering, and compositing workflows.
• Strong fundamentals in typography, composition, color, hierarchy, timing, easing, rhythm, pacing, and animation principles.
• Experience developing storyboards, style frames, motion tests, and animatics that clearly communicate an approach before production.
• Experience integrating animation with live-action footage through compositing, tracking, masking, keying, and screen replacement.
• Ability to translate complex products, systems, data, and technical concepts into clear and engaging visual communication.
• Experience building reusable motion templates and maintaining organized, production-ready project files.
• Strong communication and collaboration skills, including the ability to explain design choices, incorporate feedback, and work effectively with creative and technical partners.
• Excellent attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple assignments, versions, and deadlines in a fast-moving production environment.
• Experience with robotics, autonomy, aviation, logistics, hardware, infrastructure, healthcare, or another technically complex field is a plus.
• Experience with CAD-derived assets, product visualization, simulation, UI animation, data visualization, Lottie, Rive, Unreal Engine, or real-time workflows is a plus.
• Familiarity with emerging animation, compositing, and AI-assisted creative tools is a plus.

You’ll Thrive in the Role If:

• You are a hands-on maker who enjoys moving from early frames and motion tests through polished final animation.
• You use motion to direct attention, explain how something works, and strengthen a story.
• You are curious about complex technology and diligent about representing it accurately.
• You collaborate well with producers, editors, designers, and technical subject-matter experts.
• You respond constructively to feedback and can iterate while maintaining craft and consistency.
• You care about organized files, reliable handoffs, and the production details that make creative work reusable.
• You are passionate about Zipline’s mission, impact, and products.

What Else You Need To Know

Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities.

Whatever your decision, it will not be considered in the hiring process or thereafter. Any information that you do provide will be recorded and maintained in a confidential file.

As set forth in Zipline ’s Equal Employment Opportunity policy, we do not discriminate on the basis of any protected group status under any applicable law.

• Maintain on-set media integrity through consistent camera settings, timecode and metadata practices, card management, verification, and documented handoff to the Editor.
• Review footage with the Editor and communicate relevant continuity, exposure, color, coverage, and technical considerations for post-production.
• Contribute to practical camera tests, equipment guides, checklists, and capture workflows that improve repeatability across productions.

What You'll Bring

• A strong reel and portfolio demonstrating visual storytelling, camera and lighting craft, and range across controlled and field production, with your role identified for each project.
• Deep proficiency with professional cinema camera systems such as ARRI, RED, Sony, Canon, or Blackmagic, and the ability to adapt quickly to other systems.
• Strong knowledge of lenses, filtration, exposure, monitoring, color science, LUTs, codecs, frame rates, timecode, camera movement, and production workflows.
• Demonstrated experience designing and executing lighting and grip setups in studios and on location.
• Experience working as a solo operator, with a small crew, and within larger camera and lighting departments.
• Strong documentary instincts and the ability to anticipate action, find meaningful moments, and build useful editorial coverage in uncontrolled environments.
• Experience capturing interviews, products or hardware, demonstrations, events, and observational footage.
• Strong equipment, media, metadata, and handoff discipline.
• Clear communication and the ability to work effectively with producers, editors, engineers, operators, customers, executives, and production crews.
• Sound judgment around location conditions, access, safety requirements, schedules, and the practical limits of a production plan.
• Ability and willingness to travel approximately 30% for productions and work occasional early mornings, evenings, or weekends when production schedules require it.
• Experience capturing robotics, autonomy, aviation, logistics, manufacturing, healthcare, infrastructure, or another technically complex subject is a plus.
• Experience with high-speed capture, long-lens tracking, stabilized remote cameras, gimbals, motion control, time-lapse, aerial cinematography, or FAA Part 107 operations is a plus.

You’ll Thrive in the Role If:

• You can move between carefully controlled setups and fast documentary capture without losing attention to image quality.

• You are curious about complex technology and diligent about documenting it accurately and safely.
• You collaborate well with producers, editors, production crews, and technical subject-matter experts.

jobs.title: Senior Modeling & Simulation Engineer: National Security Missions
jobs.description:
K2 is building the largest and highest-power satellites ever flown, unlocking performance levels previously out of reach across every orbit. Backed by over $1 billion in total funding from leading investors including Altimeter Capital, ICONIQ, Kleiner Perkins, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Redpoint Ventures, and T. Rowe Price — and with over $1 billion in signed contracts across commercial and US government customers, we're mass-producing the highest-power satellite platforms ever built for missions from LEO to deep space.

The rise of heavy-lift launch vehicles is shifting the industry from an era of mass constraint to one of mass abundance, and we believe this new era demands a fundamentally different class of spacecraft. Engineered to survive the harshest radiation environments and to fully capitalize on today's and tomorrow's massive rockets, K2 satellites deliver unmatched capability at constellation scale and across multiple orbits.

With multiple launches in 2027 and plans to scale to 100 satellites a year, we're Building Bigger — helping develop the solar system and build toward a Kardashev Type II (K2) civilization. If you are a motivated individual who thrives in a fast-paced environment and you're excited about contributing to the success of a high-growth Series D-funded company, we'd love for you to apply.

The Role

You will build the modeling and simulation capabilities that let us design, verify, and operate spacecraft for demanding national security missions. You will simulate and verify the software that flies and orchestrates some of the largest satellites ever flown, and model how those systems perform against real mission objectives, threats, and operational constraints. As a senior member of the team, you will drive solutions end-to-end across the software stack, make changes to vehicle control software where needed, set technical direction, and mentor other engineers.

In your first 3 months you will generalize our simulation tools to operate in classified contexts, modeling multiple spacecraft and mission profiles, demonstrating robust performance in contested and demanding environments. In your first 6 months you will design many-agent, mission-level simulations and tools for operating entire constellations, directly informing mission assurance and critical company and program decisions.

This role supports classified national security programs. Work is performed on-site in a secure environment and requires an active TS/SCI clearance and US citizenship.

Responsibilities

• Develop mission-level modeling and simulation of national security space missions, capturing operational objectives, environments, and constraints.

• Model and analyze constellation-level capability and performance against mission requirements, including network coverage, beam planning, and resilience in contested environments.

• Support work on classified programs in accordance with all applicable security requirements.

• Create and maintain simulation software infrastructure for our 20kW+ spacecraft.

• Develop physics-based software models of spacecraft subsystems, including propulsion, attitude control, power, and communications systems.

• Create and utilize robust tools to allow for rapid deployment of quality code.

• Perform data analysis and anomaly investigation to identify and resolve on-orbit problems.

• Support integration and testing of spacecraft subsystems.

• Set technical direction, review designs and code, and mentor junior engineers.

Qualifications

• Active TS/SCI clearance, or a TS/SCI held within the last 12 months, and US citizenship.

• Prior experience working on classified national security programs and in secure/SCIF environments, including familiarity with handling classified information and program security protocols.

• Bachelor's degree in physics, aerospace/mechanical/electrical engineering, computer science, math, or a STEM field

• 5+ years of professional modeling and simulation experience.

• Development experience in Rust, C++, or similar compiled language.

• Experience using scientific Python (NumPy, SciPy, etc.), Julia, MATLAB, or similar.

• Demonstrated ability to own complex systems end-to-end and guide the work of other engineers.

Nice to Have

• Master's or PhD in physics, aerospace/mechanical/electrical engineering, computer science, math, or a STEM field.

• Experience with mission-level or campaign-level modeling and simulation for defense or national security applications.

• Facility communicating intuition and expertise effectively to stakeholders.

• Experience working in Rust production environments.

• Experience defining and creating simulation systems.

• Experience with Monte Carlo simulations and probability/statistics.

• Experience with linear algebra, controls, and/or orbital mechanics.

• Experience with space communication modeling (RF, ground stations).

• Basic knowledge of electronics, Linux, and computer architecture.

• Experience with continuous integration and continuous delivery systems.

Compensation and Benefits:

• Base salary range for this role is $160,000 - $200,000 + equity in the company

• Salary will be based on several factors including, but not limited to: knowledge and skills, education, and experience level

• Comprehensive benefits package including paid time off, medical/dental/vision/ coverage, life insurance, paid parental leave, and many other perks

If you don’t meet 100% of the preferred skills and experience, we encourage you to still apply! Building a spacecraft unlike any other requires a team unlike any other and non-traditional career twists and turns are encouraged!

If you need a reasonable accommodation as part of your application for employment or interviews with us, please let us know.

Export Compliance

As defined in the ITAR, “U.S. Persons” include U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents (i.e., Green Card holders), and certain protected individuals (e.g., refugees/asylees, American Samoans). Please consult with a knowledgeable advisor if you are unsure whether you are a “U.S. Person.”

The person hired for this role will have access to information and items controlled by U.S. export control regulations, including the export control regulations outlined in the International Traffic in Arms Regulation (ITAR). The person hired for this role must therefore either be a “U.S. person” as defined by 22 C.F.R. § 120.15 or otherwise eligible for a federally issued export control license.

Equal Opportunity

Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About Anthropic

Anthropic's mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About Beneficial Deployments

Beneficial Deployments ensures AI reaches and benefits the communities that need it most. We partner with nonprofits, governments, and mission-driven organizations to deploy Claude in education, global health, economic mobility, and life sciences.

About the Role:

We're looking for a Partnerships Manager to help extend Anthropic's health work into US public health. Building on our existing global health portfolio, you'll help shape how we engage the US public health system and manage a set of partnerships across federal, state, and local levels. Because this is an emerging area for the team, the role blends partnership management with meaningful contribution to strategy.

The right person combines credibility in the US public health ecosystem, enough technical fluency to be a real thought partner on AI deployment, and comfort operating in a space that's still taking shape.

This role is distinct from our Account Executive function: while AEs drive scaled adoption of Anthropic's core products, Partnership Managers build deep partnerships that require custom deployments, research collaboration, and hands-on program design. You'll work with a smaller portfolio of flagship partners where the goal is driving impact metrics and creating learnings that benefit the broader ecosystem.

Responsibilities:

• Contribute to Anthropic's US public health strategy, working closely with the team lead to identify priority partners and use cases and bringing field insights back to inform our broader health work

• Own a portfolio of flagship deployments, coordinating with Applied AI, product, policy, and GTM teams to deliver impact

• Source, evaluate, and onboard new partners; structure engagements that work within government procurement, data governance, and privacy constraints

• Translate partner needs into deployment plans that account for legacy systems and workforce realities

• Support the creation of shared resources and digital public goods that help the broader field use AI responsibly

• Build the evidence base by partnering with academic and evaluation organizations to study what works

• Represent Anthropic at public health convenings and with funders and policymakers

• Help shape team processes as we grow this area; hand off opportunities better suited to scaled sales or public sector motions

• Travel to partner sites and to SF headquarters every ~6 weeks for those based outside SF (~20% travel)

You Might Be a Good Fit If You Have:

• 10+ years of experience in US public health, health policy, or public sector health innovation

• 5+ years managing external partnerships, multi-stakeholder initiatives, or programs that span government and civil society

• Deep relationships and credibility in the US public health ecosystem — you know the key players at CDC, state health departments, major schools of public health, and the foundations that fund this work

• A working understanding of how federal, state, and local public health agencies operate, fund programs, and adopt new technology

• Technical fluency to engage credibly on AI concepts, understand LLM capabilities and limitations, and partner effectively with technical teams

• Experience building programs or portfolios in early-stage environments where the playbook is still being written

• High agency and comfort with ambiguity; you thrive when the playbook doesn't exist yet

• A genuine drive to strengthen the public health system and the communities it serves

• An MPH or related credential

Strong Candidates May Also Have:

• Experience inside a federal or state health agency (CDC, HHS, a state DOH) or at an organization that works closely with them

• Background in epidemiology, ideally with hands-on surveillance experience at a state, local, or federal health agency

• Experience working in a global context

• Experience at a healthtech company, AI organization, or in a product-adjacent role

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:

$300,000—$365,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. jobs.title: Propulsion Engineer II - Hardware and Bus Systems
jobs.description:
About Varda

Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules. Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.

From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.

Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.

Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.

Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.

About This Role

As the Propulsion Engineer II – Hardware & Bus Systems, you will be a hands-on technical owner of the propulsion subsystem and propulsion hardware across Varda's fleet of spacecraft. You will help own and maintain the system architecture, generate analysis products, perform component sizing, propulsion software tool development, data review, detailed mechanical design, subsystem test, operations, and more for vehicles both on the ground and in orbit.

You will take ownership of assigned systems and work products within a fast-moving interdisciplinary engineering team. Your work will directly contribute to the development of current and future vehicles key to Varda's growth. You'll thrive in a hands-on environment, building technical breadth and steadily raising the bar on everything you touch.

Responsibilities

• Support and maintain the Varda spacecraft propulsion system technical baseline, including P&IDs and system-level documentation

• Design, analyze, and test Varda satellite bus propulsion flight hardware and components

• Help scope and execute propulsion system block upgrades on operational vehicles — inclusive of both schematic and hardware changes — to increase reliability and launch cadence

• Support definition of requirements and high-level propulsion architecture for future Varda vehicles; contribute to project plans, roadmaps, and milestones

• Generate propulsion performance analysis products and document key requirements (propellant budgets, pressure ladders, fluid component sizing, structural & thermal limits, and more); deliver your outputs as key inputs to GNC, Mission Operations, Thermal, and other cross-disciplinary partner teams

• Build Python scripts and spreadsheet tools to automate recurring analysis and test data review workflows

• Execute detailed mechanical design of propulsion hardware and fluid system components; perform structural analysis using ANSYS, NASTRAN, or equivalent FEA tools

• Author and review design documentation, engineering specs, build/integration/test procedures, and engineering memos

• Support in-flight propulsion operations, including console support under senior engineer oversight

• Disposition hardware nonconformances; support anomaly investigations and contribute to corrective actions

Basic Qualifications

• B.S. in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related discipline; equivalent professional experience considered (typically 1–3+ years)

• 3+ years of hands-on experience in propulsion or fluid systems design, build, and/or test for spacecraft or launch vehicles

• Working knowledge of flight fluid system hardware: pressurized components, tubing, fittings, seals, valves, and instrumentation

• Ability to read P&IDs; experience authoring P&IDs is a plus

• Proficiency with CAD tools (e.g., CATIA, SolidWorks, NX) and PLM software

• Experience authoring or executing operational procedures for ground test or flight campaigns

• Demonstrated ability to take ownership of assigned technical tasks and drive them to resolution

Preferred Skills and Experience

• 3+ years of spacecraft or launch vehicle propulsion experience, including familiarity with satellite bus-level propulsion architectures (monopropellant, bipropellant, cold gas systems)

• Experience building Python scripts or spreadsheet tools to automate propulsion analysis or data review workflows

• Exposure to structural analysis using ANSYS, NASTRAN, or equivalent FEA tools applied to propulsion or fluid system hardware

• Familiarity with technical drawing review and GD&T per ASME Y14.5 standards

• Exposure to spacecraft-grade propellants including cryogenic, hypergolic, or high-test peroxide systems; awareness of cleanliness, handling, and safety requirements

• Test, launch site, or in-flight operational experience on spacecraft or launch vehicles

• Familiarity with 1D fluid modeling & analysis tools (GFSSP, REFPROP, or similar)

• Strong technical communication skills- clarity and precision in work instructions, engineering specs, and engineering memos

ABOUT LUMILENS

At Lumilens we are building the critical photonics infrastructure that powers tomorrow’s AI supercomputing. From chip-to-chip optical interconnects to scalable photonic engines, Lumilens is unlocking a new era of computing faster, cooler, and massively more efficient.

 
We’re a well-funded startup backed by Mayfield and led by veterans who’ve built and scaled some of the most transformative technologies in the industry. This isn’t incremental innovation, it’s a ground-floor opportunity to rethink the optical layer from the silicon up. You’ll work alongside a team of world-class engineers solving some of the hardest challenges in optics, systems, and scale. Every line of code, every design decision, every breakthrough you help deliver will shape the infrastructure of tomorrow. 
 
If you're looking for mission, momentum, and the chance to make an outsized impact jump on the rocket ship. We’re just getting started. 



POSITION OVERVIEW

We are seeking an experienced Die Attach & Wire Bond Process Technician to support semiconductor and photonics assembly processes in both NPI and production environments.

The technician will work closely with Process Engineers, Manufacturing, and Quality teams to support die attach, epoxy dispensing, curing, wire bonding, process setup, equipment operation, troubleshooting, process qualification, and production ramp activities.

The successful candidate should be hands-on, detail-oriented, and comfortable working with precision assembly equipment, process documentation, and controlled manufacturing environments.



What You'll Do:

 - Support die attach and wire bonding operations, including machine setup, recipe loading, tooling change, and process monitoring.

 - Perform epoxy dispensing, die placement, curing, wire bonding, and visual inspection according to approved procedures.

 - Support NPI builds, process trials, DOE, qualification runs, and production ramp activities under engineering guidance.

 - Perform equipment troubleshooting, preventive maintenance, and process parameter verification.

 - Conduct or support die shear, wire pull, ball shear, and other process quality checks.

 - Record process data, defects, equipment issues, and test results accurately.

 - Support engineers in yield improvement, root-cause analysis, material evaluation, and process optimization.

 - Willing to support shift work or production ramp activities when required.

Requirements & Qualifications

 - Experience with semiconductor packaging, optical modules, silicon photonics, or optical transceiver manufacturing.

 - Experience with Au wire bonding.

 - Experience with conductive or non-conductive die attach epoxy.

 - Experience with eutectic die bonding. 

 - Familiarity with die shear, wire pull, ball shear, and visual inspection criteria.

 - Basic understanding of SPC, process capability, DOE, and manufacturing process control.

 - Experience supporting NPI, engineering builds, qualification lots, or production ramp.

 - Experience with equipment brands such as K&S, Besi, Palomar, Datacon, Nordson, or similar semiconductor assembly equipment is an advantage.



Why Join Us?

This is more than a job. It's a chance to get in on the ground floor of a well-funded company set to disrupt a multi-billion dollar market. You will have the autonomy to make a massive impact, the resources to execute your vision, and a significant stake in the company you help build.

Clearance:  Active Secret Clearance

Work Location:  Arlington, VA

Responsibilities and/or Success Factors:

• Conduct thorough assessments of security controls on DSCA’s information systems and networks to ensure compliance with federal regulations, including NIST, FISMA, and DoD directives.

• Develop and maintain assessment documentation, including Security Assessment Plans (SAPs), Security Assessment Reports (SARs), and Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&Ms).

• Perform risk assessments to identify potential security threats and vulnerabilities.

• Provide detailed recommendations to mitigate identified risks and enhance the security posture of DSCA’s information systems.

• Collaborate with system owners, IT staff, and cybersecurity teams to ensure effective implementation of security controls.

• Conduct continuous monitoring activities to ensure ongoing compliance with security policies and procedures.

• Provide guidance on the security assessment and authorization (A&A) process, including developing and maintaining System Security Plans (SSPs).

• Assist in the development and delivery of cybersecurity training and awareness programs for DSCA personnel.

• Stay current with the latest cybersecurity threats, trends, and technologies to continuously improve assessment methodologies and practices.

• Participate in security audits and reviews to ensure adherence to established security standards and best practices.

Minimum Qualifications Including Certificates:

• Must be a US Citizen.

• Must have a Secret Clearance

• Bachelor's degree in Cybersecurity, Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field (Master's degree preferred).

• Minimum of 5 years of experience in information security, with a focus on security control assessment and risk management.

• Certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CISA, CAP, or equivalent are highly desirable.

• In-depth knowledge of federal cybersecurity regulations and standards, including NIST SP 800 series and FISMA.

• Proven experience in conducting security control assessments and developing security assessment documentation.

• Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.

• Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to effectively communicate complex cybersecurity concepts to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

• Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment.

Desired Qualifications:

• eMASS, cloud, STIGS experience

jobs.title: Director of User Experience
jobs.description:
Our people are our greatest differentiator at Second Nature. To build an industry-changing business, we don’t just need talent; we need an environment where high standards, continuous improvement, and customer obsession are the default.

Excellence is not a destination; it is how we show up every day. In twenty years time, we want every single employee to look back to their time at Second Nature and say: This is where I did my very best work. Where I grew the most. Where I pushed myself beyond what was comfortable. ✨





💟 ABOUT US

Today, we live in a world where everything has become convenient. Now you can get a ride anywhere, buy anything, answer any question with just a couple clicks on your phone. Convenience isn't a luxury, it's an expectation.

So why not renting? It's still a chore to get utilities set up, buy renters insurance, get air filters changed, handle pest control, and more.

That's why we've built the world's first Resident Experience Platform that makes resident onboarding, resident services, and ancillary revenue effortless for property managers.

We're passionate about turning friction into triple win experiences for residents, property managers, and investors. That way renting can be easy and rewarding for everyone.

And now you can join us. Apply today to join 300+ passionate, creative people who strive to make a difference each day so residents, property managers, and investors all win; creating the ultimate Triple Win. 🔥🔥🔥





📝 ABOUT THE ROLE

Second Nature helped define resident experience as a category in property management. 2,500+ property management companies run on our platform, we've delivered over 2 million resident experiences, and we've been named NARPM Affiliate of the Year seven times. Holding that position depends on whether the experience is genuinely better at every touchpoint.

Our experience surfaces touch Resident Onboarding, the Resident Benefits Package and the services inside it; Maestro™, our experience orchestrator; and the internal tooling our operations teams run on. Every decision has to account for the property manager, resident and the people who support them.


AI is now part of how we build: product managers explore concepts, engineers can produce interfaces and content, and our design system lets either of them ship. We want a design leader who uses that speed and still defends a high bar of what great design, content and interaction looks like.


You will lead content and user experience, reporting to the VP of Product, managing a team of 4-6 across product domains and strategic initiatives. We work in the "Product Trio" model, and your team embeds into the leadership structure of each team it works with, operating as a strategic counterpart to product and engineering leadership across multiple product areas rather than a single stream. You'll also partner directly with Customer Success, Implementation, and Data leaders, who depend on these experiences as much as our customers do.

This role is a strategic player-coach position (roughly 80% leadership & team development, 20% hands-on strategic design direction). Your hands-on contribution focuses on high-level framing, experience architecture, and driving design sprints for ambiguous, high-stakes new product surfaces.




WHAT YOU'LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR

 - The Experience Vision. A cohesive UX strategy and North Star for the Resident Experience Platform, aligned to company and product strategy.

 - Design Culture. Critique that improves the work, cross-functional collaboration, and knowledge sharing. You raise the UX bar across the whole company through coaching, workshops, and design share-outs, not just inside your team.

 - The team's growth & development. Hiring, Growth plans, leveling, compensation conversations, and feedback delivered early enough to be useful.

 - A design portfolio of your own. Named strategic projects, carried end to end.

 - The Design System. Tokens, patterns, accessibility standards, governance, and an adoption number you report on.

 - The Research Practice. Who we talk to to drive the most leverage, how often, and how evidence reaches a decision. Including what we learn that contradicts our thinking.

 - Content Design. Supporting the practice alongside interaction and visual craft.

 - The AI UX/Content operating model. Tooling, risk tiering, guardrails, and demonstrable examples that show whether it's meeting outcomes.



WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

Within 90 days. Know each designer's strengths and blind spots, with growth plans established. Publish a design coverage map: where support is real, where it's thin, what you'd trade off. Finish a design system audit with a component inventory, adoption baseline per surface, and the biggest sources of drift ranked by cost.

By six months. Design system adoption up on net-new UI across resident and property-manager surfaces, with a refined contribution model engineers/pm use without needing to route everything through your team.  A research cadence with residents and property managers that produces evidence teams cite in decisions. Published risk-tiering criteria, with a measured split of async versus full review and a rework rate you watch. Your first strategic project delivered.

By twelve months. Measurable movement on resident onboarding completion, move-in satisfaction, and support deflection, along with a fourth metric you and the domain product leads agree on. Lower time-on-task across our highest-volume internal operations workflows. A shorter path from problem framing to testable prototype, with rework flat or down.




ABOUT YOU

 - 8+ years in digital product UX, with 3+ years managing designers directly.

 - Current craft. You still design, and you can show recent work you made yourself.

 - Evidence you grow people. We'll ask you to name someone you leveled up, what you did, and where they are now.

 - Design systems at the architecture level. How tokens and patterns compose, how contribution works when it's distributed, how you hold drift down without becoming a gate.

 - The ability to look at a body of UX or content work and say what's strong, what's derivative, and what level it maps to.

 - Measurement. You define the metric before the work starts, instrument it, and change course when it moves the wrong way.

 - Executive communication. You can put UX strategy, tradeoffs, and outcomes in front of the exec team and explain what design decisions do to business metrics and the Triple Win.

 - Research leadership. You can build a practice: a repeatable cadence of talking to residents and property managers, usability testing before launch, behavioral data used to decide.

 - A position on AI and design, covering both the product surface and your team's own practice.

 - Hands-on with AI tooling. Prototyping, content, research synthesis, or design-system compliance on real shipped work.

 - You don't hold your biases too closely, and you know when to compromise.

 - Range across consumer and operator design. Residents and property managers want different things, and a leader fluent in one register risks underserving the other.


We get it. Requirements can sometimes hold people back from applying to a job, but don't let that be the case here. If you believe you have the skills it takes to elevate this role, team, and company, we encourage you to apply for this role.




REMOTE WORK STATEMENT

This position is a remote-first, work from home position. Second Nature is committed to creating a culture and workplace where remote work fosters collaboration and connections and is a key part of our company story and success. To be successful in a remote work role at Second Nature you must:

 - Be available during your scheduled working hours and give your full attention to the completion of your Second Nature job duties

 - Have a quiet, professional, distraction-free environment in which to complete your work

 - Have access to your own reliable high-speed internet connection

 - Attend our bi-annual in-person company meetings (Second Nature will reimburse the cost of your business travel per company guidelines)



Our Core Values

🏴‍☠️ Pirate Ship; not a cruise ship. Bias towards action.
💪 Massive Growth takes massive growth. We embrace challenges to increase our impact.
🥧 Grow the Pie. We focus on results so our customers & their customers win. Triple Win!
💜 Purple Heart. We put the team before ourselves.
🤝 Extreme Ownership. See something? Say something; right the ship to get us back on course.
🙌 Be a moment maker. We aim to shatter the status quo.




WHY SECOND NATURE?

 - 🩺 Health First: Medical, Dental, Vision, & Life Insurance; 401K Plan

 - 📍 Location: Work Remotely from anywhere in the US

 - 📆 Flexibility: Open PTO and sick days

 - 🤩 Culture: Diverse, inclusive, supportive, and growth-focused

 - 🚀 Growth: Be part of a fast-growing team building a new category and making a real difference

 - 💻 The Product: Award-winning, customer-loved platform that truly delivers on our mission




Second Nature is an Equal Opportunity Employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind. We take action to ensure equal employment opportunities for all candidates and employees and to provide employees with a workplace free of discrimination and harassment. Our hiring decisions are based on business needs, job requirements and individual qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion or belief, family or parental status, or any other status protected by federal and/or state law.

jobs.title: Sales & Retention Specialist
jobs.description:
About the Role

As the Retention, Onboarding & Outside Sales Lead, you own the commercial life of a premium student from the moment they buy to the moment they consider leaving. Our masteries run from $4,000 to $6,000 and higher, and three things decide whether that revenue stays: how honestly they were sold to, how well they were onboarded, and how well we handle the conversation when they ask for their money back.

This is an ownership role, not a caseload. You will run the retention conversations that matter, manage the external sales partners who bring students in, and treat onboarding as the stage that prevents refunds rather than the handoff before them. You will work AI-assisted every day, with call transcription, case summarisation and reporting handled by our tools so your attention goes to the conversations and the judgement calls. You are expected to find why cases arrive, change the system that produces them, and prove the change worked. This role suits someone who wants a number they can move and the authority to move it.

Responsibilities


Retention & Loyalty

 - Own the Number: Own the end-to-end retention process for premium programs, and own the retention rate and retained-value targets attached to it.

 - Frontline Conversations: Run retention calls personally on high-value and complex cases, and set the script, standard and coaching for anyone covering the queue.

 - Offer Ladder: Own what we offer, against which root cause and in what order, and revise it on evidence rather than instinct.

 - Experimentation: Design and run structured retention experiments each quarter: state the hypothesis, define the sample, report the result, adopt or discard.

 - Friction Removal: Identify and remove friction in the refund journey, with the authority to change intake, routing and tooling in consultation with CX and Tech.

 - Win-Back: Own the re-engagement motion for churned students and convert the win-back list into future cohort revenue.

Onboarding & Customer Experience

 - Onboarding Standard: Own onboarding as a measured stage, defining what a student should have done, understood and felt by the end of week one and week two.

 - Early Warning: Build risk signals into onboarding so disengaging students are identified before they reach the refund form.

 - Promise vs Delivery: Close the gap between what was sold and what is delivered, bringing divergence to Product and Marketing with evidence rather than anecdote.

 - Escalated Support: Deliver empathetic, high-judgement support on escalated cases through Zendesk and email, resolving them without leaving customers waiting.

 - Root Causes: Work cross-functionally with Product, Tech and Community to fix the causes behind recurring complaints, not just the instances.

Outside Sales & Agency Management

 - Agency Ownership: Own the commercial relationship with external sales and appointment-setting agencies end to end: sourcing, benchmarking, interviewing, negotiating rates and commission, contracting and ongoing management.

 - Performance Standards: Define and enforce the metrics agencies are held to, including connect rate, booked calls per hour, show rate and close rate on booked calls.

 - Internal Benchmark: Maintain our own numbers against the same metrics, so we can judge whether an agency is an improvement or a cost.

 - Sales Verification: Verify agency-claimed sales against our systems before they reach Finance, and own that reconciliation.

 - Lead Supply: Own the lists that feed outside sales, including failed payments, abandoned checkouts and churned students, and report on what they convert.

Data, Reporting & Enablement

 - Sales Enablement: Partner with internal and external closers on content training, objection handling, one-pagers, pricing clarity and QA of the booking flow.

 - Data Integrity: Own the retention dataset. Offer made, refund reason, call outcome and case status are complete and accurate on close; this is a condition of the role, not an administrative extra.

 - Reason Taxonomy: Maintain a refund-reason taxonomy specific enough to act on, keeping unclassified cases to a minimum.

 - Leadership Reporting: Present retention, onboarding and outside sales performance to leadership monthly, in person, with your own analysis and recommendations.

 - Product Feedback Loop: Turn churn reasons into named issues for Product and Marketing, with evidence and follow-through on whether anything changed.

 - Living Documentation: Maintain the Retention DNA, call scripts and transcript library as working documents, not archives.

Technical Competencies

 - Retention strategy: understanding of churn drivers, save offers, win-back mechanics and lifetime value in a high-ticket environment.

 - Commercial management: ability to source, benchmark, negotiate with and hold external sales partners to performance standards.

 - Sales strategy: conversion techniques, funnel optimisation, objection handling and customer decision psychology.

 - Data fluency: able to build and interrogate a dataset, design a valid test, read the result honestly and act on it; confident in Airtable and Google Sheets.

 - AI-assisted working: comfortable using AI daily for transcription, case analysis and reporting, and keen to push what it can take off your plate.

 - CRM & tooling: proficiency with CRM platforms, ticketing systems (Zendesk) and scheduling tools.

Soft Competencies

 - Ownership: treats the number as theirs, brings problems with a proposed answer attached, and does not wait to be asked.

 - Customer-Centricity: deep empathy, sound judgement on sensitive cases, and the integrity to do right by the customer even when it costs a save.

 - Sales Influence: clear, compelling communication that inspires action, with colleagues as readily as with customers.

 - Commercial Backbone: comfortable holding an external partner, or an internal team, to a number.

 - Problem Solving: goes after root causes rather than symptoms, and closes the loop on whether the fix worked.

 - Calm at Volume: composed when case volume spikes around cohort launches and refund windows.

Experience

 - 5+ years in retention, customer success or customer-facing sales, with at least two years owning a commercial outcome.

 - Demonstrable track record of moving a retention, churn or conversion metric, with the numbers to show it.

 - Experience managing agencies, contractors or vendors against performance standards.

 - Experience designing and running structured tests rather than only executing a process.

 - Experience with online learning platforms, high-ticket programmes and international customer bases.

 - A strong personal interest in personal growth and development (familiarity with Mindvalley content is a distinct advantage).



Mindvalley is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, colour, religion, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, marital status, sexual orientation, or any other legally protected status. We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace and encourage applications from all qualified individuals.

jobs.description:
The Nuclear Company is the fastest growing AI tech-enabled startup in the nuclear and energy space, pioneering a fleet-scale approach to building the next generation of nuclear reactors. Through our design-once, build-many model, we're accelerating the deployment of safe, reliable, and affordable nuclear energy.

We operate with an AI-first mindset. Every employee is expected to leverage AI, technology, and the Nuclear Operating System (NOS) as integral components of their role to improve the quality, speed, and impact of their work. We expect every team member to continuously identify opportunities to automate workflows, enhance decision-making, improve processes, and contribute to the ongoing evolution of NOS as a strategic operating capability that enables The Nuclear Company to scale with excellence.

We hire people who are driven by purpose, thrive in ambiguity, and are energized by building what has never been built before. Our team combines intellectual curiosity with high agency, embraces candid feedback and continuous learning, and holds themselves and others to exceptional standards. Our values—Transparency, Responsibility, Unity, Scrappiness, and Tenacity—guide how we hire, collaborate, and make decisions every day. They are not words on a wall; they are the standard by which we operate. TRUST is the foundation of our safety culture, fostering intellectual honesty, accountability, and open communication, while our values challenge every team member to execute with urgency, humility, resilience, and an unwavering commitment to our mission.

About the role

The Document Controller is responsible for managing and organizing all engineering and construction-related documentation for a large-scale infrastructure project operating within the project’s Common Data Environment and coordinating with contractor and vendor document control teams. Works closely with the project team to ensure that document management processes, numbering conventions, and metadata standards are followed by project members. Implement policies and procedures with direction from the Manager of Document Management and the Project Management Office. The Document Controller will maintain the Electronic Document Management System (EDMS) and ensure that project documents are up-to-date, properly classified and labeled, and accurately tracked from issue to closeout.

Responsibilities

• Maintain the EDMS to meet the needs of the project, assist project staff in using the system, provide training to new employees

• Manage formal transmittals between the project team, engineering, contractors, subcontractors, and vendors

• Monitor document review and comment resolution workflows to ensure timely completion

• Maintain protocols for tracking document revisions

• Maintain and enforce project document numbering conventions, metadata, and classification standards

• Ensure that project staff use document templates to maintain consistency and accuracy

• Respond to requests for up-to-date documentation including drawings, specifications, procedures, and policies

• Synthesize archived and current project documentation, archive project drawings, specifications, policies, and procedures per the archiving schedule

• Support redline and as-built documentation processes and prepare document sets and work packages

• Conduct regular audits of document management systems to ensure policies and procedures have been followed

• Collaborate with IT teams and stakeholders to ensure that project staff keep documents, document systems, and data secure

Experience

• 3 – 5 years of document control experience in large engineering, construction, or infrastructure projects

• Deep understanding of document control best practices

• Familiarity with document control software and systems, and Microsoft 365 ecosystem

• Knowledge of engineering and construction terminology and processes

• Experience applying document numbering conventions, metadata standards, and classification and taxonomy schemes in large capital projects

• Knowledge of records retention and disposition best practices

• Understanding of NRC/DOE regulatory frameworks, NQA-1, ISO 9001, and electronic record keeping standards is preferred

Benefits

• Medical, dental, vision plans

jobs.title: Per Diem Certified Nurse Midwife (CNM)
jobs.description:
Oula delivers maternity care built around our patients—offering comprehensive support before, during, and after pregnancy. With fewer C-sections and higher VBAC success rates, our research-backed approach is delivering better outcomes. Our team of trusted midwives, OBGYNs, and dedicated care navigators ensure our patients get the type of care they need in the moments that matter most.

Since launching in 2021, we’ve expanded to include Preconception and Miscarriage Care, Pregnancy Care, Postpartum Support, and Gynecology. We currently have 4 clinics in the tri-state area, with three new clinics opening in 2026! Come join our team of clinicians, innovators, operators, and technologists passionate about setting a new standard in maternity care.

Oula is seeking a Per Diem Midwife to join our growing maternity care practice in the Cotswold neighborhood. This role is ideal for a thoughtful, clinically strong midwife who is passionate about delivering patient-centered, judgment-free care and excited to practice within a collaborative, team-based care model.

As a Per Diem Midwife, you will provide full-scope midwifery care across the perinatal continuum while working closely with midwives, obstetricians, nurses, and other care team members to deliver high-quality, evidence-informed care. You will play an important role in bringing Oula’s clinical care model to life while contributing to a supportive and inclusive patient experience.

This is a  Per Diem position with a need for flexible scheduling that includes full scope clinical care (prenatal care, gynecology, labor and birth, postpartum care) and rotating on-call support of our in-hospital labor and birth care. All Oula babies will be delivered at Novant Health Presbyterian Medical Center.

Key Responsibilities

Clinical Care

• Provide full-scope, evidence-informed midwifery care, including gynecologic, prenatal, intrapartum, and postpartum care

• Deliver care across outpatient clinics, hospital-based settings, and virtual visits

• Support physiologic labor and birth while recognizing when escalation or consultation is indicated

• Collaborate closely with obstetricians, nurses, medical assistants, doulas, care coordinators, and other interdisciplinary team members to provide whole-person care

• Communicate clearly and compassionately with patients during and between visits to address questions, concerns, and care planning

• Utilize digital tools and clinical platforms to document care, support patient engagement, and coordinate with the broader care team

Collaboration & Quality

• Participate in team meetings, clinical case reviews, and quality improvement initiatives

• Adhere to clinical protocols, safety standards, and evidence-based guidelines

• Engage in chart reviews, peer feedback, and continuing education to support high-quality care

• Identify clinical concerns, system gaps, or patient safety issues and escalate appropriately

• Contribute to a positive, respectful, and inclusive team culture

About You

• Are passionate about providing compassionate, patient-centered midwifery care

• Value collaboration and thrive in interdisciplinary care environments

• Practice with empathy, professionalism, and strong clinical judgment

• Are committed to reproductive justice, body autonomy, self-determination, and culturally respectful care

• Are excited to be part of a growing maternity care practice and contribute to its success

Desired Experience & Qualifications

• Active North Carolina licensure as a Certified Nurse-Midwife and AMCB certification

• Experience providing full-scope continuity of midwifery care from outpatient clinic to in hospital birth preferred

• Experience caring for diverse patient populations with a wide range of clinical and social needs

• Strong professional references and a reputation for providing high-quality, patient-centered care

• Experience with telemedicine or virtual care delivery preferred

Preferred Skills

• Early pregnancy loss options counseling and medical management

• Familiarity with Perinatal Mental Health

• Basic bedside sonography skills (1st Trimester Viability and positioning confirmation)

Hourly Rate

$67.00 USD
